## Mascot

Tween, the on-site mascot (spec `mascot/mascot.md`, rubric `mascot/mascot_eval.md`, evidence `mascot/eval-results/`, owner notes `mascot/OWNER-NOTES.md`). Everything Tween says is written content in `content/mascot.json`; no model is called anywhere.

**Libraries: none added.** The character is a rigged inline SVG (the brand shapes and colours from `brand/tween-mascot.svg`) animated with CSS transforms and the individual `rotate`/`translate` properties; a registered CSS property (`--walk`) eases the walk cycle in and out. No animation library. The state machine, movement planner, dialogue runner and limits are small pure TypeScript modules in `lib/mascot/` (unit-tested). Lazy Tween chunk: 25.1 KB gzip (budget 30 KB); the loader module is about 0.4 KB.

**Movement.** Tween moves only along the bottom edge (a horizontal transform on a fixed element). To point it scrolls the target under the header, then picks a stand-point from the gutter beside the content or a bottom corner that does not overlap the target's text, forms or calls to action (`planPoint`), walks there, points, and rings the target with a fixed spotlight that follows scroll and resize. It goes home a few seconds after the last line. Roaming is desktop (768 px and up), motion allowed, not paused and not "Do not roam"; elsewhere it stays docked and still points (arm up) and rings the target. If a focused control would sit under Tween it steps to the other side while that element has focus (WCAG 2.4.11).

**Voice.** Off by default, opt-in, browser `speechSynthesis` only, and the toggle exists only where the browser can speak. Nothing is ever spoken without a user action: the greeting, the tip and the nudge are never spoken (tested with a counter on `speak`).

**Deviations from `mascot.md`, and why**

1. *Delivery.* The layout renders a ~0.4 KB loader; after the page `load` and idle it fetches `/api/mascot` (a static same-origin JSON route) and the lazy chunk together. Passing the copy as props from the layout would have put it in every page's RSC payload. If either fails Tween is absent.
2. *`pet` moved out of `system.json`* into `content/mascot.json` (the old prototype is removed; the three route-tip lines that carried an unsourced time ("about two minutes") or pointed at the Trust page were rewritten).
3. *Seven entry points, four choices per node.* The root offers four buttons (pilot, work, cost, "More options"); the other entry points are one step further. The cap of four is enforced by the schema.
4. *Schema additions.* A node may have `variants` (by build fact: published work, preview slots, hidden or shown prices) and the two token lines `{tip}` and `{priceLines}`. Prices are never typed in the content: the server builds the lines from the same function the Plans page uses (`priceLineText`), so hidden mode yields no number and the priced fixture yields exactly the numbers in `plans.json`.
5. *No AI statements (owner instruction, mid-build).* There is no "How do you use AI?" entry point and no node links to `/trust`; a test fails if the word AI appears in Tween's copy. The one allowed fact about narration ("We use AI models for voice narration, and manual narration is also supported") is not used because Tween has no free-text input to answer a narration question.
6. *Lead flow asks one more question than the spec lists:* the form requires a role, so the chat asks name, work email, company website, what to make (one choice; the form allows several), role, then consent. Validation is the form's own function and copy (`LEAD_ERROR_MESSAGES` was moved into `lib/lead-fields.ts` so both use one source). The time-trap start is when the chat flow started.
7. *Prefill.* "Open the full form" writes the answers (never consent) to `sessionStorage`; the form reads them once and removes them immediately, so nothing personal stays in storage (spec: "cleared on submit"; this is stricter). The chat transcript stores only Tween's lines and the label "Answer given".
8. *Events.* New names in `lib/tracking.ts`: `tween_open`, `tween_choice`, `tween_hide`, `tween_lead_start`, `tween_lead_submit`. A completed chat request also fires the existing `form_submit` once with `source: "tween"` so funnels still see it.
9. *Unprompted limits interact.* One per page view means that a first visit to `/plans` or `/work` gets the idle nudge instead of the greeting (the greeting would use up the page view before 45 s). The nudge, the tip and the greeting are each once per session; three per session in all.
10. *Layout shift.* Chrome counts movement of fixed elements, so the panel is laid out whole when a choice is made (unsaid lines and the reply buttons are hidden, not absent), is anchored by its top edge and lifted with a transform, and is moved sideways with transforms only. Result: zero layout shift attributed to Tween in tests, and Lighthouse CLS unchanged (0).
11. *Accessible names.* Tween's pause button is "Pause Tween" because the hero loop already has a "Pause animation" button; two buttons with one name was caught by an existing test.
12. *Developer hook.* `?tween=<state>` (with `&dir=left|right|up`, `&panel=1`) works in preview and test builds only; it is guarded by `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_MODE !== "production"` and a test proves the production-mode fixture ignores it.
13. *Lightbox.* "Show me work" with published work says its line first, then opens the first published item in the existing lightbox; Tween is hidden while the lightbox, the mobile menu or a form is in view.
14. *Placeholder markers.* Because the AI node was removed, `content/mascot.json` currently carries no markers of its own; the unit tests inject one to prove the lint, the preview tolerance and the production refusal all cover this file.
15. *Git.* The tree contained another agent's uncommitted edits to shared files (layout, `LeadForm`, `Section`, schemas, content). Only files that are wholly Tween's were committed; the mascot hunks in shared files are listed in `mascot/CHANGELOG.md` and left for the owner to commit together.

## Mascot redesign (Tween, v2)

The owner supplied a hand-drawn image of a preferred Tween (rounder navy body, peacock-feather morpankh, tapered limbs, paddle hands). It was redrawn as vector parts in `components/mascot/TweenRig.tsx`, keeping the rig's class names, joints and CSS pose variables so all ten poses and the movement code carry over unchanged. The brand now has one teal and gold accent, used only on the feather (`#119C9A`, `#F3B63A`, `#F26A21`); the site UI palette is unchanged. Static brand art (`brand/tween-*.svg/.png`, `public/brand/`) is exported from the same component by `scripts/render-tween-brand.mjs`, so the logo mascot and the animated one cannot drift apart. The favicon was redrawn to match. The likeness is a redraw by eye, not a trace: the glossy feather shading is simplified to flat layers.
